title: Vedāntasāra — Complete Sanskrit Reader
author: Sadānanda Yogīndra
coverage: Complete local Sanskrit text including prose and all 38 numbered source passages; opening verses 1 and 2 are separate units. Each of the 71 entries has Sanskrit, transliteration, an English translation, and a word-for-word gloss.

source.edition: Sadānanda Yogīndra's Vedāntasāra; checked against the Sanskrit Wikisource text.
source.changes: One opening source unit containing verses 1 and 2 is separated into two verse cards. The complete Sanskrit text and its source numbering are retained. Original English translations and word-for-word lexical glosses are provided for all 71 entries.

units.label: Verse 1
units.deva: अखण्डं सच्चिदानन्दमवाङ्मनसगोचरम्। आत्मानमखिलाधारमाश्रयेऽभीष्टसिद्धये॥१॥
units.translation: I seek refuge in the indivisible Self, existence-consciousness-bliss, beyond the reach of speech and mind, the support of all, for the fulfillment of the desired end.

gloss.en: beyond the reach of speech and mind
for fulfillment of the desired end

units.label: Verse 2
units.deva:
अर्थतोऽप्यद्वयानन्दानतीतद्वैतभानतः।
गुरूनाराध्य वेदान्तसारं वक्ष्ये यथामति॥२॥
units.translation: Having revered the teachers, whose very nature is bliss beyond duality and who are beyond the appearance of duality, I shall set forth the essence of Vedānta as far as I am able.

gloss.en: those who are bliss beyond duality
because they transcend the appearance of duality

units.label: Passage 3
units.deva:
अनुबन्धचतुष्टयम्
वेदान्तो नामोपनिषत्प्रमाणं तदुपकारीणि शारीरकसूत्रादीनि च। अस्य वेदान्तप्रकरणत्वात्तदीयैरेवानुबन्धैस्तद्वत्तासिद्धेर्न ते पृथगालोचनीयाः। तत्रानुबन्धो नामाधिकारिविषयसम्बन्ध प्रयोजनानि॥३॥
units.translation: The four preliminary matters are stated here. Vedānta means the Upaniṣads, which are the means of knowledge, together with supporting works such as the Brahma Sūtras. Since this is a Vedānta treatise, its status is established by those same preliminary matters; they need not be examined separately. Those matters are the qualified student, the subject, the relation, and the purpose.

gloss.en: the Upaniṣads as a means of knowledge
the Brahma Sūtras and other works
because it is a Vedānta treatise
by those belonging to it alone
because its status as such is established
the qualified student, subject, relation, and purpose

units.label: Prose 3
units.deva: अधिकारी तु विधिवदधीतवेदवेदाङ्गत्वेनापाततोऽधिगताखिल-वेदार्थोऽस्मिन् जन्मनि जन्मान्तरे वा काम्यनिषिद्धवर्जनपुरःसरं नित्य-नैमित्तिकप्रायश्चित्तोपासनानुष्ठानेन निर्गतनिखिलकल्मषतया नितान्त-निर्मलस्वान्तः साधनचतुष्टयसम्पन्नः प्रमाता ।
units.translation: The qualified student is an inquirer who has properly studied the Veda and its auxiliary disciplines and gained an introductory understanding of the entire meaning of the Veda; who, in this birth or a previous one, first gave up desire-driven and forbidden acts, and performed daily and occasional duties, expiatory rites, and contemplation; who has thereby become free of every impurity, has an exceedingly pure heart, and is endowed with the four qualifications.

gloss.en: by having studied the Veda and its auxiliary disciplines
having understood the whole meaning of the Veda
with abandoning desire-driven and forbidden acts as the first step
through performing daily duties, occasional duties, expiatory rites, and contemplation
by becoming free from every impurity

units.label: Prose 4
units.deva: काम्यानि स्वर्गादीष्टसाधनानि ज्योतिष्टोमादीनि। निषिद्धानि नरकाद्यनिष्ट-साधनानि ब्राह्मणहननादीनि । नित्यान्यकरणे प्रत्यवायसाधनानि सन्ध्यावन्दनादीनि। नैमित्तिकानि पुत्रजन्माद्यनुबन्धीनि जातेष्ट्यादीनि। प्रायश्चित्तानि पापक्षयसाधनानि चान्द्रायणादीनि। उपासनानि सगुण-ब्रह्मविषयमानसव्यापाररूपाणि शाण्डिल्यविद्यादीनि। एतेषां नित्यादीनां बुद्धिशुद्धिः परं प्रयोजनमुपासनानां तु चित्तैकाग्र्यं “तमेतमात्मानं वेदानुवचनेन ब्राह्मणा विविदिषन्ति यज्ञेन ”  इत्यादिश्रुतेः “तपसा कल्मषं हन्ति” इत्यादि स्मृतेश्च। नित्य नैमित्तिक प्रायश्चित्तोपासनानां त्ववान्तरफलं पितृलोकसत्यलोकप्राप्तिः "कर्मणा पितृलोको विद्यया देवलोक"  इत्यादिश्रुतेः।
units.translation: Desire-driven rites are means to desired results such as heaven, for example the Jyotiṣṭoma. Forbidden acts lead to unwanted results such as hell, for example killing a Brahmin. Daily duties, such as twilight worship, cause a fault when omitted. Occasional duties, such as birth rites, are connected with events such as the birth of a son. Expiatory rites, such as the Cāndrāyaṇa, remove sin. Contemplative practices, such as the Śāṇḍilya meditation, are mental activities directed toward Brahman with attributes. The primary result of daily duties and the like is clarity of understanding, while contemplation produces steadiness of mind. Scripture says that Brahmins seek to know the Self through Vedic recitation and sacrifice; remembered teaching says that austerity destroys impurity. An intermediate result of daily, occasional, expiatory, and contemplative practices is attainment of the world of the ancestors or the world of Brahmā, as scripture teaches.

gloss.en: means to desired results such as heaven
means to unwanted results such as hell
killing a Brahmin and similar acts
connected with events such as the birth of a son
means for the removal of sin
mental activities directed toward Brahman with attributes
the Śāṇḍilya meditation and similar practices
and from remembered teaching beginning thus
of daily, occasional, expiatory, and contemplative practices
attainment of the world of the ancestors or Brahmā

units.label: Prose 5
units.deva: साधनानि नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकेहामुत्रार्थफलभोगविरागशमादिषट्क-सम्पत्तिमुमुक्षुत्वानि। नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकस्तावद् ब्रह्मैव नित्यं वस्तु ततोऽन्यदखिलमनित्यमिति विवेचनम्। ऐहिकानां स्रक्चन्दनवनितादि-विषयभोगानां कर्मजन्यतयानित्यत्ववदामुष्मिकाणामप्यमृतादिविषय-भोगानामनित्यतया तेभ्यो नितरां विरतिरिहामुत्रार्थफलभोगविरागः।
units.translation: The four qualifications are discrimination between the eternal and the non-eternal, dispassion toward enjoyment of the fruits of action here and hereafter, the sixfold discipline beginning with tranquillity, and the desire for liberation. Discrimination means discerning that Brahman alone is eternal and everything else is non-eternal. Just as worldly enjoyments—garlands, sandalwood, women, and the like—are impermanent because they arise from action, so too the otherworldly enjoyments of objects such as immortality are impermanent. Complete withdrawal from them is dispassion toward the fruits enjoyed here and hereafter.

gloss.en: discrimination between the eternal and non-eternal
dispassion toward fruits enjoyed here and hereafter
the sixfold discipline beginning with tranquillity
discrimination between the eternal and non-eternal
enjoyments of objects such as garlands, sandalwood, and women
enjoyments of objects such as immortality
dispassion toward fruits enjoyed here and hereafter

units.label: Prose 6
units.deva: शमादयस्तु शमदमोपरतितितिक्षासमाधानश्रद्धाख्याः। शमः तावच्छ्रवणादिव्यतिरिक्तविषयेभ्यो मनसो निग्रहः। दमो बाह्येन्द्रियाणां तद्-व्यतिरिक्तविषयेभ्यो निवर्तनम्। निवर्तितानामेतेषां तद्-व्यतिरिक्तविषयेभ्य उपरमणमुपरतिरथवा विहितानां कर्मणां विधिना परित्यागः। तितिक्षा शीतोष्णद्वन्द्वसहिष्णुता। निगृहीतस्य मनसः श्रवणादौ तदनुगुणविषये च समाधिः समाधानम् । गुरूपदिष्ट-वेदान्तवाक्येषु विश्वासः श्रद्धा। मुमुक्षुत्वं मोक्षेच्छा। एवम्भूतः प्रमाताधिकारी "शान्तो दान्त" इत्यादिश्रुतेः।
units.translation: The six disciplines are tranquillity, sense-restraint, withdrawal, endurance, collectedness, and trust. Tranquillity is control of the mind away from objects other than those involved in hearing the teaching and related practices. Sense-restraint is turning the external senses away from other objects. Withdrawal is the resting of these restrained senses from those objects, or the prescribed renunciation of ritual acts. Endurance is bearing pairs of opposites such as heat and cold. Collectedness is the mind, once restrained, being fixed on hearing and other appropriate subjects. Trust is confidence in the Vedānta statements taught by the teacher. The desire for liberation is longing for liberation. Such an inquirer is qualified, as scripture says, “peaceful, self-controlled.”

gloss.en: called tranquillity, sense-restraint, withdrawal, endurance, collectedness, and trust
from objects other than hearing and related practice
bearing the pair of opposites, heat and cold
in Vedānta statements taught by the teacher

units.label: Passage 4
units.deva: विषयो जीवब्रहौक्यं शुद्धचैतन्यं प्रमेयं तत्रैव वेदान्तानां तात्पर्यात्। सम्बन्धस्तु तदैक्यप्रमेयस्य तत्प्रतिपादकोपनिषत्प्रमाणस्य बोध्यबोधक-भावः। प्रयोजनं तु तदैक्यप्रमेयगताज्ञाननिवृत्तिः स्वस्वरूपानन्दावाप्तिश्च "तरति शोकमात्मवित्" इत्यादिश्रुतेः "ब्रह्मविद् ब्रह्मैव भवति"  इत्यादि श्रुतिश्च॥४॥
units.translation: The subject is the identity of the individual self and Brahman, pure consciousness, because that is the Upaniṣads’ central teaching. The relation is that of what is to be understood to the Upaniṣadic means of knowledge that teaches this identity. The purpose is the removal of ignorance concerning this identity and the attainment of the bliss that is one’s own nature, as scripture says, “the knower of the Self crosses sorrow” and “the knower of Brahman becomes Brahman itself.”

gloss.en: the identity of the individual self and Brahman
of the Upaniṣadic means of knowledge that teaches it
the relation of what is to be understood and what teaches it
removal of ignorance about that identity
attainment of the bliss that is one’s own nature

units.label: Passage 5
units.deva: अयमधिकारी जननमरणादिसंसारानलसन्तप्तो प्रदीप्तशिरोजल-राशिमिवोपहारपाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठं गुरुमुपसृत्य तमनुसरति "समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठं" इत्यादिश्रुतेः। स गुरुः परम-कृपयाध्यारोपापवादन्यायेनैनमुपदिशति "तस्मै स विद्वानुपसन्नाय प्राह "  इत्यादि श्रुतेः॥५॥
units.translation: This qualified student, scorched by the fire of worldly existence—birth, death, and the rest—approaches a teacher who has studied the Veda and is established in Brahman, like one carrying water to extinguish a blaze upon one’s own head, and follows the teacher, as scripture says, “with fuel in hand, approach a teacher learned in the Veda and established in Brahman.” Out of supreme compassion, the teacher instructs the student by the method of superimposition and rescission, as scripture says, “to that student who has approached, the wise one spoke.”

gloss.en: scorched by the fire of worldly existence beginning with birth and death
like water carried to extinguish a blaze on one’s head
by the method of superimposition and rescission

units.label: Passage 6
units.deva:
अज्ञाननिरूपणम्
असर्पभूतायां रज्जौ सर्पारोपवद्वस्तुन्यवस्त्वारोपोऽध्यारोपः। वस्तु सच्चिदानन्दानन्ताद्वयं ब्रह्म। अज्ञानादिसकलजडसमूहोऽवस्तु। अज्ञानं तु सदसद्भ्यामनिर्वचनीयं त्रिगुणात्मकं ज्ञानविरोधि भावरूपं यत्किञ्चिदिति वदन्त्यहमज्ञ इत्याद्यनुभवात् "देवात्मशक्तिं स्वगुणैर्निगूढाम्" इत्यादिश्रुतेश्च॥६॥
units.translation: Superimposition is placing what is unreal upon a real thing, as when a snake is imagined on a rope that is not a snake. The real is Brahman, existence-consciousness-bliss, infinite and non-dual. The unreal is ignorance and the entire collection of inert things. Ignorance is said to be something indescribable as either existent or non-existent, made of the three qualities, opposed to knowledge, and positive in nature; this is known from the experience “I am ignorant” and from scripture declaring that the divine power is concealed by its own qualities.

gloss.en: like the superimposition of a snake
the whole collection of inert things beginning with ignorance
having the three qualities as its nature
the divine power of the Self

units.label: Prose 10
units.deva: इदमज्ञानं समष्टिव्यष्ट्यभिप्रायेणैकमनेकमिति च व्यवह्रियते। तथाहि यथा वृक्षाणां समष्ट्यभिप्रायेण वनमित्येकत्वव्यपदेशो यथा वा जलानां समष्ट्यभिप्रायेण जलाशय इति तथा नानात्वेन प्रतिभासमानानां जीव-गताज्ञानानां समष्ट्यभिप्रायेण तदेकत्वव्यपदेशो “अजामेकाम्” इत्यादिश्रुतेः।
units.translation: This ignorance is spoken of as one or many according to the collective or individual standpoint. For example, trees considered collectively are called a forest in the singular; likewise, waters considered collectively are called a reservoir. In the same way, the ignorance belonging to individual selves, though appearing as many, is spoken of as one from the collective standpoint, as in the scriptural statement “the one unborn.”

gloss.en: from the collective and individual standpoints
of ignorance belonging to individual selves

units.label: Prose 11
units.deva: इयं समष्टिरुत्कृष्टोपाधितया विशुद्धसत्त्वप्रधाना। एतदुपहितं चैतन्यं सर्वज्ञत्वसवेश्वरत्वसर्वनियन्तृत्वादिगुणकमव्यक्तमन्तर्यामी जगत्कारणम् ईश्वर इति च व्यपदिश्यते सकलाज्ञानावभासकत्वात्। “यः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित्" इति श्रुतेः ईश्वरस्येयं समष्टिरखिलकारणत्वात् कारण-शरीरमानन्दप्रचुरत्वात् कोशवदाच्छादकत्वाच्चानन्दमयकोशः, सर्वोप-रमत्वात्सुषुप्तिरत एव स्थूलसूक्ष्मप्रपञ्चलयस्थानमिति चोच्यते।
units.translation: This collective ignorance is predominantly pure in sattva because it has a superior limiting adjunct. The consciousness associated with it is described as the unmanifest, the inner controller, and Īśvara, the cause of the world, endowed with omniscience, lordship over all, and control of all, because it illumines all ignorance. Scripture says, “the one who knows all, who knows everything.” This collective aspect of Īśvara is the causal body because it is the cause of all; it is the sheath of bliss because it is full of bliss and covers like a sheath; and it is deep sleep because all things withdraw into it. Therefore it is also called the place where the gross and subtle worlds dissolve.

gloss.en: because of a superior limiting adjunct
endowed with omniscience, lordship over all, control of all, and other qualities
because it is the cause of all
the place where the gross and subtle worlds dissolve

units.label: Passage 7
units.deva: यथा वनस्य व्यष्ट्यभिप्रायेण वृक्षा इत्यनेकत्वव्यपदेशो यथा वा जलाशयस्य व्यष्ट्यभिप्रायेण जलानीति तथाज्ञानस्य व्यष्ट्यभिप्रायेण तदनेकत्वव्यपदेश “इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुरूप ईयत" इत्यादिश्रुतेः। अत्र व्यस्तसमस्त-व्यापित्वेन व्यष्टिसमष्टिताव्यपदेशः। इयं व्यष्टिर्निकृष्टोपाधितया मलिन-सत्त्वप्रधाना। एतदुपहितं चैतन्यमल्पज्ञत्वानीश्वरत्वादिगुणकं प्राज्ञ इत्युच्यत एकाज्ञानावभासकत्वात्। अस्य प्राज्ञत्वस्पष्टोपाधितयानति-प्रकाशकत्वात् अस्यापीयमहङ्कारादिकारणत्वात् कारणशरीरमानन्द-प्रचुरत्वात् कोशवदाच्छादकत्वाच्चानन्दमयकोशः, सर्वोपरमत्वात् सुषुप्तिरत एव स्थूलसूक्ष्मशरीरप्रपञ्चलयस्थानमिति चोच्यते॥७॥
units.translation: Just as trees are called many when viewed individually within a forest, and waters are called many when viewed individually within a reservoir, so ignorance is called many from the individual standpoint, as scripture says, “Indra appears in many forms through his powers of māyā.” The terms “individual” and “collective” apply because the same reality pervades the parts and the whole. This individual aspect is predominantly impure in sattva because its limiting adjunct is inferior. The consciousness associated with it is called Prājña, characterized by limited knowledge and lack of lordship, because it illumines one individual ignorance. Because this limiting adjunct makes it not shine clearly, and because it is the cause of ego and the rest, this individual aspect is the causal body, the sheath of bliss, and deep sleep, where the gross and subtle body-world dissolves.

gloss.en: because it pervades the parts and the whole
the designation as individual and collective
because of an inferior limiting adjunct
characterized by limited knowledge, lack of lordship, and the like
because it illumines one individual ignorance
because its adjunct makes its character as Prājña evident
because it does not shine clearly
because it is the cause of ego and the rest
and because it covers like a sheath
the place where the gross and subtle body-world dissolves

units.label: Passage 8
units.deva:
प्राज्ञेश्वरनिरूपणम्
तदानीमेतावीश्वरप्राज्ञौ चैतन्यप्रदीप्ताभिरतिसूक्ष्माभिरज्ञानवृत्तिभिरानन्दमनुभवत "आनन्दभुक् चेतोमुखः प्राज्ञ" इति श्रुतेः । सुखमहमस्वाप्सं न किञ्चिद् अवेदिषमित्युत्थितस्य परामर्शोपपत्तेश्च। अनयोः समष्टिव्यष्ट्योः वनवृक्षयोरिव जलाशयजलयोरिव वाभेदः। एतदुपहितयोरीश्वर-प्राज्ञयोरपि वनवृक्षावच्छिन्नाकाशयोरिव जलाशयजलगतप्रतिबिम्बाका-शयोरिव वाभेद "एष सर्वेश्वर" इत्यादि श्रुतेः॥८॥
units.translation: At that time, Īśvara and Prājña experience bliss through very subtle mental modifications illumined by consciousness, as scripture says, “Prājña, whose doorway is the mind, enjoys bliss.” This is also supported by the waking person’s recollection, “I slept happily; I knew nothing.” The collective and individual aspects are non-different, like a forest and its trees or a reservoir and its waters. Likewise, Īśvara and Prājña, consciousness associated with these two aspects, are non-different, like the space delimited by a forest and a tree or the reflected space in a reservoir’s water, as scripture says, “This is the Lord of all.”

gloss.en: of the one who has awakened
of the space delimited by forest and tree
of the space reflected in a reservoir’s water

units.label: Passage 9
units.deva:
तुरीयनिरूपणम्
वनवृक्षतदवच्छिन्नाकाशयोर्जलाशयजलतद्गतप्रतिबिम्बाकाशयोः वाधार-भूतानुपहिताकाशवदनयोरज्ञानतदुपहितचैतन्ययोराधारभूतं यदनुपहितं चैतन्यं तत्तुरीयमित्युच्यते "शिवमद्वैतं चतुर्थं मन्यन्त" इत्यादिश्रुतेः। इदमेव तुरीयं शुद्धचैतन्यमज्ञानादितदुपहितचैतन्याभ्यां तप्तायःपिण्ड-वदविविक्तं सन्महावाक्यस्य वाच्यं विविक्तं सल्लक्ष्यमिति चोच्यते।।९।।
units.translation: The consciousness that is not associated with ignorance, and that is the basis of both ignorance and the consciousness associated with it, is called Turīya. It is like the undelimited space that is the basis of a forest and the space delimited by trees, or of a reservoir and the reflected space in its water. Scripture says, “They regard the fourth as auspicious and non-dual.” This Turīya alone is pure consciousness. Though it appears inseparable from ignorance and the consciousness conditioned by it, like a red-hot iron ball, it is distinguished by the great Upaniṣadic sentence and is therefore called its direct meaning in one respect and its indicated meaning in another.

gloss.en: of the forest and the space delimited by its trees
of a reservoir, its water, and the space reflected there
like the undelimited space that is their basis
of ignorance and consciousness associated with it
from ignorance and consciousness associated with it

units.label: Prose 15
units.deva:
शक्तिद्वयनिरूपणम्
अस्याज्ञानस्यावरणविक्षेपनामकरमस्ति शक्तिद्वयम्। आवरणशक्तिः तावदल्पोऽपि मेघोऽनेकयोजनायतमादित्यमण्डलमवलोकयितृनयन-पथपिधायकतया यथाच्छादयतीव तथाज्ञानं परिच्छिन्नमप्यात्मानम् अपरिच्छिन्नमसंसारिणमवलोकयितृबुद्धिपिधायकतयाच्छादयतीव तादृशं सामर्थ्यम्। तदुक्तम् –
units.translation: This ignorance has two powers, called concealment and projection. The power of concealment works like a small cloud that seems to cover the sun, which is many leagues across, by blocking the observer’s line of sight. In the same way, ignorance seems to cover the Self, though it is indivisible, unlimited, and free from worldly existence, by obscuring the observer’s understanding. Such is its capacity. This is expressed in the following verse.

gloss.en: an explanation of the two powers
by blocking the observer’s line of sight

units.label: Prose 16
units.deva:
"घनच्छन्नदृष्टिर्घनच्छन्नमर्कं यथा मन्यते निष्प्रभं चातिमूढः। 
तथा बद्धवद्भाति यो मूढदृष्टेः स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा " इति ॥
units.translation: “As a person of clouded vision thinks the sun, hidden by clouds, is dim, so the Self, whose nature is ever-present awareness, appears bound to one whose vision is confused.”

gloss.en: one whose sight is obscured by clouds

units.label: Passage 10
units.deva: अनयैवावरणशक्त्यावच्छिन्नस्यात्मनः कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वसुखदुःखमोहात्म-कतुच्छसंसारभावनापि सम्भाव्यते यथा स्वाज्ञानेनावृतायां रज्ज्वां सर्पत्व-सम्भावना। विक्षेपशक्तिस्तु यथा रज्वज्ञानं स्वावृतरज्जौ स्वशक्त्या सर्पादिकमुद्भावयत्येवमज्ञानमपि स्वावृतात्मनि विक्षेपशक्त्याकाशादि-प्रपञ्चमुद्भावयति तादृशं सामर्थ्यम्। तदुक्तम् "विक्षेपशक्तिर्लिङ्गादि ब्रह्माण्डान्तं जगत्सृजेद्" इति॥१०॥
units.translation: Because of this power of concealment, the Self, appearing limited, may seem to be an agent and enjoyer and to be subject to pleasure, pain, delusion, and other low worldly states, just as a rope covered by one’s ignorance may be mistaken for a snake. The power of projection works as follows: just as ignorance of a rope projects a snake and the like upon the rope it conceals, ignorance projects the world beginning with space upon the Self it conceals. This capacity is stated in the verse: “The power of projection creates the world from the subtle body up to the cosmic egg.”

gloss.en: the idea of worldly existence as agent, enjoyer, pleasure, pain, delusion, and the like
the supposition that it is a snake
upon the rope it has covered
upon the Self it has covered

units.label: Passage 11
units.deva:
कारणनिरूपणम्
शक्तिद्वयवदज्ञानोपहितं चैतन्यं स्वप्रधानतया निमित्तं स्वोपाधि-प्रधानतयोपादानं च भवति। यथा लूता तन्तुकार्यं प्रति स्वप्रधानतया निमित्तं स्वशरीरप्रधानतयोपादानं च भवति॥११॥
units.translation: Consciousness associated with ignorance, which has these two powers, is the efficient cause because consciousness is primary, and the material cause because its limiting adjunct is primary. A spider, for example, is the efficient cause of its web through itself and its material cause through its own body.

gloss.en: because its limiting adjunct is primary
because its own body is primary

units.label: Passage 12
units.deva: तमःप्रधानविक्षेपशक्तिमदज्ञानोपहितचैतन्यादाकाश आकाशाद्वायुः वायोरग्निरग्नेरापोऽद्भ्यः पृथिवी चोत्पद्यते "तस्माद्वा एतस्मादात्मन आकाशः सम्भूत" इत्यादिश्रुतेः। तेषु जाड्याधिक्यदर्शनात्तमःप्राधान्यं तत्कारणस्य। तदानीं सत्त्वरजस्तमांसि कारणगुणप्रक्रमेण तेषु आकाशादिषूत्पद्यन्ते। एतान्येव सूक्ष्मभूतानि तन्मात्राण्यपञ्चीकृतानि चोच्यन्ते। एतेभ्यः सूक्ष्मशरीराणि स्थूलभूतानि चोत्पद्यन्ते॥१२॥
units.translation: From consciousness associated with ignorance, whose power of projection is dominated by tamas, space arises; from space, air; from air, fire; from fire, water; and from water, earth, as scripture says, “From this Self arose space.” Because inertness is most evident in these elements, their cause is dominated by tamas. At that stage, sattva, rajas, and tamas arise in space and the other elements in the order of the qualities of their cause. These are called subtle elements, rudiments, and uncombined elements. From them arise the subtle bodies and the gross elements.

gloss.en: from consciousness associated with ignorance, whose projecting power is dominated by tamas
in the order of the qualities of the cause
in space and the other elements

units.label: Prose 20
units.deva:
सूक्ष्मशरीरम्
सूक्ष्मशरीराणि सप्तदशावयवानि लिङ्गशरीराणि। अवयवास्तु ज्ञानेन्द्रिय-पञ्चकं बुद्धिमनसी कर्मेन्द्रियपञ्चकं वायुपञ्चकं चेति। ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि श्रोत्रत्वक्चक्षुर्जिह्वाघ्राणाख्यानि। एतान्याकाशादीनां सात्त्विकांशेभ्योः व्यस्तेभ्यः पृथक् पृथक् क्रमेणोत्पद्यन्ते। बुद्धिर्नाम निश्चयात्मिकान्तःकरण वृत्तिः। मनो नाम सङ्कल्पविकल्पात्मिकान्तःकरणवृत्तिः। अनयोरेव चित्ताहङ्कारयोरन्तर्भावः। एते पुनराकाशादिगतसात्त्विकांशेभ्यो मिलितेभ्य उत्पद्यन्ते। एतेषां प्रकाशात्मकत्वात्सात्त्विकांशकार्यत्वम्। इयं बुद्धिर्ज्ञानेन्द्रियैः सहिता विज्ञानमयकोशो भवति। अयं कर्तृत्व-भोक्तृत्वसुखित्वदुःखित्वाद्यभिमानत्वेनेहलोकपरलोकगामी व्यावहारिको जीव इत्युच्यते। मनस्तु ज्ञानेन्द्रियैः सहितं सन्मनोमयकोशो भवति।
units.translation: The subtle bodies, also called liṅga bodies, have seventeen components: the five organs of knowledge, intellect and mind, the five organs of action, and the five vital airs. The organs of knowledge are hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell. They arise separately and in order from the sattva portions of space and the other elements. Intellect is the inner-organ activity whose nature is determination. Mind is the inner-organ activity whose nature is resolving and doubting. Memory and ego are included within these two. These arise from the combined sattva portions of space and the other elements. Because they are luminous in nature, they are products of the sattva portions. Intellect together with the organs of knowledge forms the sheath of understanding. Identifying with agency, enjoyment, happiness, sorrow, and the rest, the empirical individual travels in this world and the next. Mind together with the organs of knowledge forms the sheath of mind.

gloss.en: called hearing, skin, eye, tongue, and nose
of space and the other elements
a function of the inner organ
having resolve and doubt as its nature
a function of the inner organ
from the combined sattva portions of space and the other elements
being products of the sattva portions
through identification with agency, enjoyment, happiness, sorrow, and the like
travelling in this world and the next

units.label: Prose 21
units.deva: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि वाक्पाणिपादपायूपस्थाख्यानि। एतानि पुनराकाशादीनां रजोंशेभ्यो व्यस्तेभ्यः पृथक् पृथक् क्रमेणोत्पद्यन्ते। वायवः प्राणापान-व्यानोदानसमानाः। प्राणो नाम प्राग्गमनवान्नासाग्रस्थानवर्ती। अपानो नामावाग्गमनवान् पाय्वादिस्थानवर्ती। व्यानो नाम विष्वग्गमन-वानखिलशरीरवर्ती। उदानो नाम कण्ठस्थानीय ऊर्ध्वगमनवानुत्क्रमण-वायुः। समानो नाम शरीरमध्यगताशितपीतान्नादिसमीकरणकरः।
units.translation: The organs of action are speech, hands, feet, the anus, and the genitals. They arise separately and in order from the rajas portions of space and the other elements. The five vital airs are prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna. Prāṇa moves forward and is located at the tip of the nose. Apāna moves downward and is located in the lower organs. Vyāna moves everywhere and pervades the whole body. Udāna is located in the throat, moves upward, and carries the person out at death. Samāna is located in the middle of the body and equalizes food that has been eaten and drunk.

gloss.en: called speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals
of space and the other elements
prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna
located at the tip of the nose
the air that carries one out at death
located in the middle of the body
equalizing food that has been eaten, drunk, and so on

units.label: Prose 22
units.deva: केचित्तु नागकूर्मकृकलदेवदत्तधनञ्जयाख्याः पञ्चान्ये वायवः सन्तीति वदन्ति। तत्र नाग उद्गिरणकरः। कूर्म उन्मीलनकरः। कृकलः क्षुत्करः। देवदत्तो जृम्भणकरः। धनञ्जयः पोषणकरः। एतेषां प्राणादिष्वन्तर्भावात् प्राणादयः पञ्चैवेति केचित्। एतत्प्राणादिपञ्चकमाकाशादिगतरजोंशेभ्यो मिलितेभ्य उत्पद्यते। इदं प्राणादिपञ्चकं कर्मेन्द्रियैः सहितं सत्प्राणमय-कोशो भवति। अस्य क्रियात्मकत्वेन रजोंशकार्यत्वम्।
units.translation: Some authorities say that there are five other vital airs, called Nāga, Kūrma, Kṛkala, Devadatta, and Dhanañjaya. Nāga causes belching; Kūrma causes blinking; Kṛkala causes sneezing; Devadatta causes yawning; and Dhanañjaya nourishes the body. Some say there are only the five primary airs because these five functions are included among prāṇa and the others. This group of five airs arises from the combined rajas portions of space and the other elements. Joined with the organs of action, they form the sheath of vital air. Since they are active in nature, they are products of the rajas portions.

gloss.en: called Nāga, Kūrma, Kṛkala, Devadatta, and Dhanañjaya
this group of five airs beginning with prāṇa
from the combined rajas portions of space and the other elements
group of five airs beginning with prāṇa
being a product of the rajas portions

units.label: Passage 13
units.deva: एतेषु कोशेषु मध्ये विज्ञानमयो ज्ञानशक्तिमान् कर्तृरूपः। मनोमय इच्छाशक्तिमान् करणरूपः। प्राणमयः क्रियाशक्तिमान् कार्यरूपः। योग्यत्वादेवमेतेषां विभाग इति वर्णयन्ति। एतत्कोशत्रयं मिलितं सत्सूक्ष्मशरीरमित्युच्यते॥१३॥
units.translation: Among these sheaths, the sheath of understanding has the power of knowledge and functions as the agent; the sheath of mind has the power of will and functions as the instrument; and the sheath of vital air has the power of action and functions as the effect. They are divided in this way because these roles suit them. These three sheaths together are called the subtle body.

gloss.en: having the form of an agent
having the form of an instrument
having the form of an effect

units.label: Passage 14
units.deva:
अत्राप्यखिलसूक्ष्मशरीरमेकबुद्धिविषयतया वनवज्जलाशयवद्वा समष्टिः अनेकबुद्धिविषयतया वृक्षवज्जलवद्वा व्यष्टिरपि भवति। एतत्समष्ट्युपहितं चैतन्यं सूत्रात्मा हिरण्यगर्भः प्राण श्चेत्युच्यते सर्वत्रानुस्यूतत्वाज्- ज्ञानेच्छाक्रियाशक्तिमदुपहितत्वाच्च। अस्यैषा समष्टिः स्थूलप्रपञ्चापेक्षया सूक्ष्मत्वात्सूक्ष्मशरीरं विज्ञानमयादिकोशत्रयं जाग्रद्वासनामयत्वात्स्वप्नोऽत एव स्थूलप्रपञ्चलयस्थानमिति चोच्यते। एतद्व्यष्ट्युपहितं चैतन्यं तैजसो भवति तेजोमयान्तःकरणोपहितत्वात्। अस्यापीयं व्यष्टिः स्थूल-शरीरापेक्षया सूक्ष्मत्वादिति हेतोरेव सूक्ष्मशरीरं विज्ञानमयादिकोशत्रयं जाग्रद्वासनामयत्वात्स्वप्नोऽत एव स्थूलशरीरलयस्थानमिति चोच्यते।
एतौ सूत्रात्मतैजसौ तदानीं मनोवृत्तिभिः सूक्ष्मविषयाननुभवतः “प्रविविक्तभुक्तैजस” इत्यादिश्रुतेः। अत्रापि समष्टिव्यष्ट्योस्तदुपहित-सूत्रात्मतैजसयोर्वनवृक्षवत्तदवच्छिन्नाकाशवच्च जलाशयजलतद्गत-प्रतिबिम्बाकाशवच्चाभेदः। एवं सूक्ष्मशरीरोत्पत्ति॥१४॥
units.translation: Here, too, the entire subtle body is the collective when it is the object of one cognition, like a forest or reservoir; it is the individual when it is the object of many cognitions, like trees or waters. Consciousness associated with this collective is called Sūtrātman, Hiraṇyagarbha, or Prāṇa because it runs through everything and is associated with the powers of knowledge, will, and action. Compared with the gross world, this collective aspect is the subtle body, the three sheaths beginning with the sheath of understanding, the dream state because it consists of impressions from waking, and the place where the gross world dissolves. Consciousness associated with the individual aspect is Taijasa because it is conditioned by the luminous inner organ. For the same reason, this individual aspect is also called the subtle body, the three sheaths beginning with the sheath of understanding, the dream state because it consists of waking impressions, and the place where the gross body dissolves. At that time, Sūtrātman and Taijasa experience subtle objects through mental modifications, as scripture says, “Taijasa enjoys the subtle.” Here, too, the collective and individual aspects, and Sūtrātman and Taijasa associated with them, are non-different, like a forest and its trees, the space delimited by them, a reservoir and its waters, or the reflected space in its water. Thus the subtle body arises.

gloss.en: because it is the object of one cognition
because it is the object of many cognitions
and because it is associated with the powers of knowledge, will, and action
in comparison with the gross world
the three sheaths beginning with understanding
because it consists of waking impressions
the place where the gross world dissolves
because it is conditioned by the luminous inner organ
in comparison with the gross body
the three sheaths beginning with understanding
because it consists of waking impressions
the place where the gross body dissolves
of the collective and individual aspects
of Sūtrātman and Taijasa associated with them
and like space delimited by them
and like a reservoir, its waters, and reflected space
the arising of the subtle body

units.label: Prose 25
units.deva:
पञ्चीकरणप्रक्रिया
स्थूलभूतानि तु पञ्चीकृतानि। पञ्चीकरणं त्वाकाशादिपञ्चस्वेकैकं द्विधा समं विभज्य तेषु दशसु भागेषु प्राथमिकान्पञ्चभागान्प्रत्येकं चतुर्धा समं विभज्य तेषां चतुर्णां भागानां स्वस्वद्वितीयार्धभागपरित्यागेन भागान्तरेषु संयोजनम्। तदुक्तम्
units.translation: The gross elements are formed by fivefold combination. This process takes place as follows: each of the five elements beginning with space is first divided into two equal halves. Then each first half is divided into four equal parts. Each element is combined with one half of itself and one eighth from each of the other four elements. This is stated in the following verse.

gloss.en: in the five elements beginning with space
leaving aside each element’s own second half

units.label: Prose 26
units.deva:
"द्विघा विधाय चैकैकं चतुर्धा प्रथमं पुनः। 
     स्वस्वेतरद्वितीयांशैर्योजनात्पञ्चपञ्चते” इति।।
units.translation: “Divide each one into two equal parts; then divide the first half again into four. By joining those parts with the second halves of the other elements, each becomes fivefold.”

gloss.en: with the second portions belonging to each of the other elements

units.label: Passage 15
units.deva:
अस्याप्रामाण्यं नाशङ्कनीयं त्रिवृत्करणश्रुतेः पञ्चीकरणस्याप्युप-लक्षणत्वात्। पञ्चानां पञ्चात्मकत्वे समानेऽपि तेषु च “वैशेष्यात्तद्वादस्तद्वाद" इतिन्यायेनाकाशादिव्यपदेशः सम्भवति।
तदानीमाकाशे शब्दोऽभिव्यज्यते वायौ शब्दस्पर्शावग्नौ शब्दस्पर्श-रूपाण्यप्सु शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसाः पृथिव्यां शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धाश्च॥१५॥
units.translation: The authority of this account should not be doubted because scripture mentions threefold combination; that teaching serves as an illustrative indication of fivefold combination as well. Though the five elements are all made up of five, their designation as space and the rest remains possible according to the principle “the name follows the distinctive feature.” At that time, sound becomes manifest in space; sound and touch in air; sound, touch, and form in fire; sound, touch, form, and taste in water; and sound, touch, form, taste, and smell in earth.

gloss.en: because it serves as an illustrative indication
designation as space and the rest
sound, touch, form, taste, and smell

units.label: Passage 16
units.deva:
स्थूलसृष्टिनिरूपणम्
एतेभ्यः पञ्चीकृतेभ्यो शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसाः भूतेभ्यो भूर्भुवःस्वर्महर्जनस्तपः-सत्यमित्येतन्नामकानामुपर्युपरिविद्यमानानामतलवितलसुतलरसातलतलातलमहातलपातालनामकानामधोऽधोविद्यमानानां लोकानां ब्रह्माण्डस्य तदन्तर्वर्तिचतुर्विधस्थूलशरीराणां तदुचितानामन्नपानादीनां चोत्पत्तिर्भवति।
चतुर्विधशरीराणि तु जरायुजाण्डजोद्भिज्जस्वेदजाख्यानि। जरायुजानि जरायुभ्यो जातानि मनुष्यपश्वादीनि। अण्डजान्यण्डेभ्यो जातानि पक्षिपन्नगादीनि। उद्भिज्जानि भूमिमुद्भिद्य जातानि लतावृक्षादीनि। स्वेदजानि स्वेदेभ्यो जातानि यूकामशकादीनि॥१६॥
units.translation: From these fivefold-combined gross elements arise the worlds above—Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Mahaḥ, Janaḥ, Tapaḥ, and Satya—as well as the worlds below—Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Rasātala, Talātala, Mahātala, and Pātāla. The cosmic egg arises, together with the four kinds of gross bodies within it and the foods and drinks suitable to them. The four kinds of bodies are womb-born, egg-born, sprout-born, and moisture-born. Humans, animals, and the like are womb-born; birds and serpents are egg-born; vines and trees that emerge through the earth are sprout-born; and lice, mosquitoes, and the like are moisture-born.

gloss.en: Bhūḥ, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Mahaḥ, Janaḥ, Tapaḥ, and Satya
Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Rasātala, Talātala, Mahātala, and Pātāla
of the four kinds of gross bodies
called womb-born, egg-born, sprout-born, and moisture-born

units.label: Passage 17
units.deva:
अत्रापि चतुर्विधसकलस्थूलशरीरमेकानेकबुद्धिविषयतया वनवज्जलाशय-वद्वा समष्टिर्वृक्षवज्जलवद्वा व्यष्टिरपि भवति। एतत्समष्ट्युपहितं चैतन्यं वैश्वानरो विराड् इत्युच्यते सर्वनराभिमानित्वाद्विविधं राजमानत्वाच्च। 
अस्यैषा समष्टिः स्थूलशरीरमन्नविकारत्वादन्नमयकोशः स्थूल-भोगायतनत्वाच्च स्थूलशरीरं जाग्रदिति च व्यपदिश्यते । एतद् व्यष्ट्युपहितं चैतन्यं विश्व इत्युच्यते सूक्ष्मशरीराभिमानमपरित्यज्य स्थूलशरीरादि प्रविष्टत्वात्। अस्याप्येषा व्यष्टिः स्थूलशरीरमन्नविकारत्वादेव हेतोरन्नमय-कोशो जाग्रदिति चोच्यते।
तदानीमेतौ विश्ववैश्वानरौ दिग्वातार्कवरुणाश्विभिः क्रमान्नियन्त्रितेन श्रोत्रादीन्द्रियपञ्चकेन क्रमाच्छब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धानग्नीन्द्रोपेन्द्रयम-प्रजापतिभिः क्रमान्नियन्त्रितेन वागादीन्द्रियपञ्चकेन क्रमाद्वचनादानगमन-विसर्गानन्दां चन्द्रचतुर्मुखशङ्कराच्युतैः क्रमान्नियन्त्रितेन मनोबुद्ध्यहङ्कार-चित्ताख्येनान्तरिन्द्रियचतुष्केण क्रमात्सङ्कल्पनिश्चयाहङ्कार्यचैत्तांश्च सर्वान् एतान् स्थूलविषयाननुभवतो "जागरितस्थानो बहिःप्रज्ञ" इत्यादिश्रुतेः।
अत्राप्यनयोः स्थूलव्यष्टिसमष्ट्योस्तदुपहितविश्ववैश्वानरयोश्च वनवृक्ष-वत्तदवच्छिन्नाकाशवच्च जलाशयजलवत्तद्गतप्रतिबिम्बाकाशवच्च पूर्ववद् अभेदः। एवं पञ्चीकृतपञ्चभूतेभ्यः स्थूलप्रपञ्चोत्पत्तिः।।१७।।
units.translation: Here, too, the totality of the four kinds of gross bodies is the collective when it is the object of one or many cognitions, like a forest or a reservoir; it is the individual when considered as many, like trees or waters. Consciousness associated with the collective is called Vaiśvānara or Virāj because it identifies with all people and shines in diverse forms. The collective aspect is the gross body because it is a modification of food, the sheath of food, the support of gross experience, and the waking state. Consciousness associated with the individual is called Viśva because, without giving up identification with the subtle body, it has entered the gross body and the rest. This individual aspect is likewise the gross body, the sheath of food because it is a modification of food, and the waking state. At that time, Viśva and Vaiśvānara experience all gross objects in sequence: sounds, touches, forms, tastes, and smells through the five sense organs beginning with hearing, governed respectively by the deities of the directions, wind, sun, Varuṇa, and the Aśvins; speech, taking, movement, excretion, and pleasure through the five organs of action beginning with speech, governed respectively by Agni, Indra, Upendra, Yama, and Prajāpati; and resolve, determination, ego-making, and memory through the four inner organs called mind, intellect, ego, and memory, governed respectively by the moon, the four-faced creator, Śaṅkara, and Acyuta. This is supported by scripture’s statement, “the waking state is outwardly cognitive.” Here, too, the individual and collective gross bodies and Viśva and Vaiśvānara associated with them are non-different, as previously explained by the examples of a forest and its trees, delimited space, a reservoir and its water, and reflected space. Thus the gross universe arises from the fivefold-combined elements.

gloss.en: the totality of the four kinds of gross bodies
as the object of one or many cognitions
because of identifying with all people
because it is a modification of food
and because it is the support of gross experience
the gross body and the rest
because it is a modification of food
by the deities of the directions, wind, sun, Varuṇa, and the Aśvins
by the five sense organs beginning with hearing
sounds, touches, forms, tastes, and smells
by Agni, Indra, Upendra, Yama, and Prajāpati
by the five organs of action beginning with speech
speaking, taking, moving, excreting, and pleasure
by the moon, four-faced creator, Śaṅkara, and Acyuta
called mind, intellect, ego, and memory
the individual and collective gross bodies
of Viśva and Vaiśvānara associated with them
like a forest and its trees
and like space delimited by them
like a reservoir and its water
and like reflected space within it
the arising of the gross universe

units.label: Passage 18
units.deva:
स्थूलमहाप्रपञ्चः
एतेषां स्थूलसूक्ष्मकारणप्रपञ्चानामपि समष्टिरेको महान्प्रपञ्चो भवति यथावान्तरवनानां समष्टिरेकं महद्वनं भवति यथा वावान्तरजलाशयानां समष्टिरेको महान् जलाशयः। एतदुपहितं वैश्वानरादीश्वरपर्यन्तं चैतन्यमप्यवान्तरवनावच्छिन्नाकाशवदवान्तरजलाशयगत-प्रतिबिम्बाकाशवच्चैकमेव। आभ्यां महाप्रपञ्चतदुपहितचैतन्याभ्यां तप्तायःपिण्ड-वदविविक्तं सदनुपहितं चैतन्यं "सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म" इति वाक्यस्य वाच्यं भवति विविक्तं सल्लक्ष्यमपि भवति। एवं वस्तुन्यवस्त्वारोपोऽध्यारोपः सामान्येन प्रदर्शितः।।१८॥
units.translation: The collective of the gross, subtle, and causal worlds is one great universe, just as several forests together form one great forest, or several reservoirs form one great reservoir. The consciousness associated with it—from Vaiśvānara through Īśvara—is also one, like the space reflected in many forests or reservoirs. The consciousness that is not associated with these two—the great universe and the consciousness conditioned by it—is undivided from them like a red-hot iron ball. It is the direct meaning of the statement “All this is indeed Brahman,” and, when distinguished from them, its indicated meaning. Thus superimposition, the attribution of the unreal to the real, has been shown in general.

gloss.en: of the gross, subtle, and causal worlds
like space delimited by smaller forests
and like reflected space within smaller reservoirs
the great universe and consciousness associated with it

units.label: Passage 19
units.deva:
चार्वाकादिमतनिराकरणम्
इदानीं प्रत्यगात्मनीदमिदमयमयमारोपयतीति विशेषत उच्यते। अतिप्राकृतस्तु “आत्मा वै जायते पुत्र" इत्यादिश्रुतेः स्वस्मिन्निव स्वपुत्रेऽपि प्रेमदर्शनात्पुत्रे पुष्टे नष्टे चाहमेव पुष्टो नष्टश्चेत्याद्यनुभवाच्च पुत्र आत्मेति वदति।
चार्वाकस्तु "स वा एष पुरुषोऽन्नरसमय" इत्यादिश्रुते: प्रदीप्तगृहात्स्वपुत्रं परित्यज्यापि स्वस्य निर्गमदर्शनात्स्थूलोऽहं कृशोऽहमित्याद्यनुभवाच्च स्थूलशरीरमात्मेति वदति।
अपरश्चार्वाकः "ते ह प्राणाः प्रजापतिं पितरमेत्य ब्रूयुः" इत्यादिश्रुतेरिन्द्रियाणामभावे शरीरचलनाभावात्काणोऽहं बधिरोऽहम् इत्याद्यनुभवाच्चेन्द्रियाण्यात्मेति वदति।
अपरश्चार्वाकः "अन्योऽन्तर आत्माप्राणमय" इत्यादिश्रुतेः प्राणाभाव इन्द्रियादिचलनायोगादहमशनायावानहं पिपासावानित्याद्यनुभवाच्च प्राण आत्मेति वदति।
अन्यस्तु चार्वाकः "अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा मनोमय" इत्यादिश्रुतेर्मनसि सुप्ते प्राणादेरभावादहं सङ्कल्पवानहं विकल्पवानित्याद्यनुभवाच्च मन आत्मेति वदति। 
बौद्धस्तु “अन्योऽन्तर आत्मा विज्ञानमय" इत्यादिश्रुतेः कर्तुरभावे करणस्य शक्तयभावादहं कर्ताहं भोक्तेत्याद्यनुभवाच्च बुद्धिरात्मेति वदति। 
प्राभाकरतार्किकौ तु "अन्योऽन्तर आत्मानन्दमय" इत्यादिश्रुते बुद्धयादीनामज्ञाने लयदर्शनदहमज्ञोऽहमज्ञानीत्याद्यनुभवाच्चाज्ञानम् आत्मेति वदतः।
भाट्टस्तु "प्रज्ञानघन एवानन्दमय" इत्यादिश्रुतेः सुषुप्तौ प्रकाशाप्रकाश-सद्भावान्मामहं न जानामीत्याद्यनुभवाच्चाज्ञानोपहितं चैतन्यमात्मेति वदति। 
अपरो बौद्धः "असदेवेदमग्र आसीत्" इत्यादिश्रुतेः सुषुप्तौ सर्वाभावादहं सुषुप्तौ नासमित्युत्थितस्य स्वाभावपरामर्शविषयानुभवाच्च शून्यमात्मेति वदति ॥१९॥
units.translation: The false views about the Self are now set out in detail: “I superimpose this, this, that, and that upon the inner Self.” The very unsophisticated person says that the son is the Self, citing “The Self is born as a son,” and because love is seen for one’s son as for oneself; when the son thrives or perishes, one says, “I myself have thrived” or “I myself have perished.” A materialist says that the gross body is the Self, citing “This person is made of the essence of food,” and because one leaves one’s own son behind in a burning house to escape and says, “I am stout” or “I am thin.” Another materialist says that the senses are the Self, citing the scripture in which the vital functions approach their father, Prajāpati, and because without the senses the body does not move; one says, “I am blind” or “I am deaf.” Another says that the vital air is the Self, citing “There is another inner Self, made of vital air,” and because without vital air the senses cannot move; one says, “I am hungry” or “I am thirsty.” Another materialist says that the mind is the Self, citing “There is another inner Self, made of mind,” and because when the mind sleeps the vital functions and the rest are absent; one says, “I intend” or “I doubt.” A Buddhist says that the intellect is the Self, citing “There is another inner Self, made of understanding,” and because instruments have no power without an agent; one says, “I act” or “I enjoy.” The Prābhākara and the logician say that ignorance is the Self, citing “There is another inner Self, made of bliss,” and because intellect and the rest are seen to resolve into ignorance; one says, “I am ignorant.” The Bhāṭṭa says that consciousness conditioned by ignorance is the Self, citing “It is a mass of knowledge, made of bliss,” and because in deep sleep there is both illumination and non-illumination; one wakes and says, “I did not know myself.” Another Buddhist says that the void is the Self, citing “All this was non-being in the beginning,” and because in deep sleep everything is absent; one wakes and recalls the experience “I was not in deep sleep.”

gloss.en: refutation of the views of the materialists and others
“the Self is indeed born as a son”
for one’s own son as well
“this person is made of the essence of food”
“the vital functions approached their father, Prajāpati, and spoke”
because the body does not move
“another inner Self, made of vital air”
because movement of the senses and the rest is impossible
because the vital functions and the rest are absent
because they are seen to resolve
“a mass of knowledge, made of bliss”
because illumination and non-illumination are present
“all this was non-being in the beginning”
I was not in deep sleep
from the experience of recollecting one’s absence

units.label: Passage 20
units.deva:
एतेषां पुत्रादीनामनात्मत्वमुच्यते। एतैरतिप्राकृतादिवादिभिरुक्तेषु श्रुतियुक्त्यनुभवाभासेषु पूर्वपूर्वोक्तश्रुतियुक्त्यनुभवाभासानामुत्तरोत्तर-श्रुतियुक्त्यनुभवाभासैरात्मत्वबाधदर्शनात् पुत्रादीनामनात्मत्वं स्पष्टमेव।
किञ्च प्रत्यगस्थूलोऽचक्षुरप्राणोऽमना अकर्ता चैतन्यं चिन्मात्रं सदित्यादिप्रबलश्रुतिविरोधादस्य पुत्रादिशून्यपर्यन्तस्य जडस्य चैतन्य-भास्यत्वेन घटादिवदनित्यत्वादहं ब्रह्मेति विद्वदनुभवप्राबल्याच्च तत्तच्छ्रुतियुक्त्यनुभवाभासानां बाधितत्वादपि पुत्रादिशून्यपर्यन्तमखिलम् अनात्मैव। अतस्तत्तद्भासकं नित्यशुद्धबुद्धमुक्तसत्यस्वभावं प्रत्यक्चैतन्यमेवात्मवस्त्विति वेदान्तविद्वदनुभवः। एवमध्यारोपः॥२०॥
units.translation: The son and the rest are said to be not-Self. The apparent scriptural statements, arguments, and experiences put forward by the very unsophisticated theorists are successively contradicted as accounts of the Self by stronger scriptural statements, arguments, and experiences; therefore the non-Self nature of the son and the rest is clear. Moreover, powerful scripture teaches that the inner Self is not gross, has no eyes, vital air, or mind, is not an agent, and is pure consciousness and reality. The inert things from the son down to the void are illumined by consciousness and impermanent like a pot. The strong experience of the wise, “I am Brahman,” also defeats those apparent scriptural statements, arguments, and experiences. Therefore everything from the son to the void is indeed not-Self. The experience of Vedānta knowers is that the inward consciousness, which illumines all of them and whose nature is eternal, pure, awakened, liberated, and real, alone is the Self. Thus superimposition has been explained.

gloss.en: the very unsophisticated theorists and the rest
apparent scriptural statements, arguments, and experiences
apparent scriptural statements, arguments, and experiences
by later and stronger scriptural statements, arguments, and experiences
because their status as Self is negated
of the son and the rest
because of contradiction by powerful scripture
extending from the son down to the void
because it is illumined by consciousness
like a pot and the rest
and because of the strength of the wise person’s experience
of those apparent scriptural statements, arguments, and experiences
from the son down to the void
that which illumines each of them
whose nature is eternal, pure, awakened, liberated, and real

units.label: Prose 33
units.deva:
अपवादनिरूपणम्
अपवादो नाम रज्जुविवर्तस्य सर्पस्य रज्जुमात्रत्ववद्वस्तुविवर्तस्यावस्तुनो अज्ञानादेः प्रपञ्चस्य वस्तुमात्रत्वम् । तदुक्तम् –
units.translation: Rescission means recognizing the unreal world—such as the snake that appears through a transformation of the rope—as nothing but the real substratum, just as the apparent snake is nothing but the rope. This is stated in the following verse.

gloss.en: of what appears as a transformation of a rope
like being nothing but the rope
of what appears as a transformation of reality

units.label: Prose 34
units.deva:
सतत्त्वतोऽन्यथाप्रथा विकार इत्युदीरितः ।
अतत्त्वतोऽन्यथाप्रथा विवर्त इत्युदीरितः ॥” इति ॥
units.translation: “A change in which something appears otherwise in reality is called a transformation; an appearance of something otherwise without being real is called an apparent transformation.”

units.label: Passage 21
units.deva:
तथाहि एतद्भोगायतनं चतुर्विधसकलस्थूलशरीरजातं भोग्य-रूपान्नपानादिकमेतदायतनभूतभूरादिचतुर्दशभुवनान्येतदायतनभूतं ब्रह्माण्डं चैतत्सर्वमेतेषां कारणरूपं पञ्चीकृतभूतमात्रं भवति । एतानि शब्दादिविषयसहितानि पञ्चीकृतानि भूतानि सूक्ष्मशरीरजातं चैतत्सर्वमेतेषां कारणरूपापञ्चीकृतभूतमात्रं भवति ।
एतानि सत्त्वादिगुणसहितान्यपञ्चीकृतान्यपञ्चीकृतान्युत्पत्तिव्युत्क्रमेण एतत्कारणभूताज्ञानोपहितचैतन्यमात्रं भवति । एतदज्ञानमज्ञानोपहितं चैतन्यं चेश्वरादिकमेतदाधारभूतानुपहितचैतन्यस्वरूपं तुरीयं ब्रह्मात्रं भवति ॥२१॥
units.translation: For example, the entire collection of four kinds of gross bodies that serves as the place of experience, the food and drink that are the objects experienced, the fourteen worlds beginning with Bhūḥ that serve as their setting, and the cosmic egg that contains them all have as their cause only the fivefold-combined elements. Those fivefold-combined elements together with their objects such as sound, and the entire collection of subtle bodies, have as their cause only the uncombined subtle elements. These uncombined elements, with the qualities beginning with sattva, when traced back in reverse order of creation, resolve into consciousness associated with the ignorance that is their cause. That ignorance, the consciousness associated with ignorance, and all such forms beginning with Īśvara resolve into Turīya Brahman, the nature of the unassociated consciousness that is their basis.

food, drink, and the rest as objects of experience
serving as the setting for them

serving as the setting for this

units.label: Passage 22
units.deva: आभ्यामध्यारोपापवादाभ्यां तत्त्वम्पदार्थशोधनमपि सिद्धं भवति। तथाहि – अज्ञानादिसमष्टिरेतदुपहितं सर्वज्ञत्वादिविशिष्टचैतन्यमेतदनुपहितं चैतत्त्रयं तप्तायःपिण्डवदेकत्वेनावभासमानं तत्पदवाच्यार्थो भवति। एतदुपाध्युपहिताधारभूतमनुपहितं चैतन्यं तत्पदलक्ष्यार्थो भवति । अज्ञानादिव्यष्टिरेतदुपहिताल्पज्ञत्वादिविशिष्टचैतन्यमेतदनुपहितं चैतत्त्रयं तप्तायःपिण्डवदेकत्वेनावभासमानं त्वम्पदवाच्यार्थो भवति। एतदुपाध्युप-हिताधारभूतमनुपहितं प्रत्यगानन्दं तुरीयं चैतन्यं त्वम्पदलक्ष्यार्थो भवति ॥२२॥
units.translation: By these two methods, superimposition and rescission, the meanings of the words “That” and “you” are also clarified. The collective of ignorance, the consciousness conditioned by it and characterized by omniscience and the like, and the unconditioned consciousness, appearing as one like a red-hot iron ball, together constitute the direct meaning of “That.” The unconditioned consciousness that is the basis of the limiting adjuncts is the indicated meaning of “That.” The individual aspect of ignorance, consciousness conditioned by it and characterized by limited knowledge and the like, and the unconditioned consciousness, appearing as one like a red-hot iron ball, together constitute the direct meaning of “you.” The inner blissful Turīya consciousness, unconditioned and the basis of those limiting adjuncts, is the indicated meaning of “you.”

gloss.en: clarification of the meanings of “That” and “you”
the collective of ignorance and the rest
consciousness characterized by omniscience and the rest
the basis of the limiting adjuncts associated with it
the individual aspect of ignorance and the rest
consciousness associated with it and characterized by limited knowledge and the rest
the basis of the limiting adjuncts associated with it

units.label: Prose 37
units.deva:
महावाक्यार्थनिरूपणम्
अथ महावाक्यार्थो वर्ण्यते। इदं तत्त्वमसिवाक्यं सम्बन्धत्रयेणाखण्डार्थबोधकं भवति । सम्बन्धत्रयं नाम पदयोः सामानाधिकरण्यं पदार्थयोर्विशेषणविशेष्यभावः प्रत्यगात्म-लक्षणयोर्लक्ष्यलक्षणभावश्चेति । तदुक्तम् –
units.translation: The meaning of the great sentence is now explained. The statement “That thou art” conveys an indivisible meaning through three relations: co-reference of the words, the relation between a qualifier and what it qualifies, and the relation between an indicator and what it indicates, namely the individual Self.

gloss.en: an explanation of the meaning of the great sentence
the meaning of the great sentence
of the meanings of the words
the relation of qualifier and qualified
of the inner Self and its indicator
the relation of what is indicated and its indicator

units.label: Prose 38
units.deva:
"सामानाधिकरण्यं च विशेषणविशेषता ।
लक्ष्यलक्षणसम्बन्धः पदार्थप्रत्यगात्मनाम् ” इति ॥
units.translation: “Co-reference, the relation of qualifier and qualified, and the relation of indicator and indicated between the meanings of the words and the inner Self [reveal the sentence’s meaning].”

gloss.en: the relation of qualifier and qualified
the relation of indicator and indicated
between the word meanings and the inner Self

units.label: Passage 23
units.deva:
सामानाधिकरण्यसम्बन्धस्तावद्यथा सोऽयं देवदत्त इत्यस्मिन्वाक्ये तत्कालविशिष्टदेवदत्तवाचक-स-शब्दस्यैतत्कालविशिष्टदेवदत्त-वाचकायंशब्दस्य चैकस्मिन्पिण्डे तात्पर्यसम्बन्धः । तथा च तत्त्वमसीति वाक्येऽपि परोक्षत्वादिविशिष्टचैतन्यवाचकतत्पदस्यापरोक्षत्वादि-विशिष्टचैतन्यवाचकत्वम्पदस्य चैकस्मिन् चैतन्ये तात्पर्यसम्बन्धः ।
विशेषणविशेष्यभावसम्बन्धवस्तु यथा तत्रैव वाक्ये सशब्दार्थ-तत्कालविशिष्टदेवदत्तस्यायं शब्दार्थैतत्कालविशिष्टदेवदत्तस्य चान्योन्य-भेदव्यावर्तकतया विशेषणविशेष्यभावः। तथात्रापि वाक्ये तत्पदार्थ-परोक्षत्वादिविशिष्टचैतन्यस्य त्वम्पदार्थापरोक्षत्वादिविशिष्टचैतन्यस्य चान्योन्यभेदव्यावर्तकतया विशेषणविशेष्यभावः ।
लक्ष्यलक्षणसम्बन्धस्तु यथा तत्रैव वाक्ये सशब्दायंशब्दयोः तदर्थयोर्वा विरुद्धतत्कालैतत्कालविशिष्टत्वपरित्यागेनाविरुद्धदेवदत्तेन सह लक्ष्य-लक्षणभावः । तथात्रापि वाक्ये तत्त्वम्पदयोः तदर्थयोर्वा विरुद्ध-परोक्षत्वापरोक्षत्वादि विशिष्टत्वपरित्यागेन अविरुद्धचैतन्येन सह लक्ष्यलक्षणभावः । इयमेव भागलक्षणा इत्युच्यते ॥२३॥
units.translation: Co-reference is illustrated by the sentence “That is this Devadatta.” The word “that” denotes Devadatta qualified by a past time, while “this” denotes Devadatta qualified by the present time; both words intend one and the same person. Likewise, in “That thou art,” the word “That” denotes consciousness qualified by remoteness and the like, while “thou” denotes consciousness qualified by immediacy and the like; their intended reference is the same consciousness. The relation of qualifier and qualified is also illustrated by this sentence: the meanings of “that” and “this,” Devadatta qualified by past and present time, respectively, exclude their mutual difference and qualify one another. Similarly, the meanings of “That” and “thou,” consciousness qualified by remoteness and immediacy, exclude mutual difference and qualify one another. The relation of indicator and indicated is also illustrated by the same sentence: when the incompatible qualifications of past and present time are given up, the words “that” and “this” indicate the non-conflicting Devadatta. Likewise, in the great sentence, when the incompatible qualifications of remoteness and immediacy are given up, “That” and “thou” indicate the non-conflicting consciousness. This is called the method of partial implication.

gloss.en: of the word “that,” denoting Devadatta qualified by a past time
of the word “this,” denoting Devadatta qualified by the present time
of the word “That,” denoting consciousness qualified by remoteness and the like
of “thou,” denoting consciousness qualified by immediacy and the like
the relation of qualifier and qualified
of Devadatta qualified by a past time
of Devadatta qualified by the present time
the relation of indicator and indicated
by giving up the incompatible qualification of past and present time
the relation of indicator and indicated

the relation of indicator and indicated

units.label: Prose 40
units.deva:
अस्मिन्वाक्ये नीलमुत्पलमिति वाक्यवद्वाक्यार्थो न सङ्गच्छते । तत्र तु नीलपदार्थनीलगुणस्योत्पलपदार्थोत्पलद्रव्यस्य च शौक्ल्यपटादिभेद-व्यावर्तकतयान्योन्यविशेषणविशेष्यभावसंसर्गस्यान्यतरविशिष्टस्यान्यत-रस्य तदैक्यस्य वा वाक्यार्थत्वाङ्गीकारे प्रमाणान्तरविरोधाभावात्तद्वाक्यार्थः सङ्गच्छते  ।
अत्र तु तदर्थपरोक्षत्वादिविशिष्टचैतन्यस्य त्वमर्थापरोक्षत्वादि-विशिष्टचैतन्यस्य चान्योन्यभेदव्यावर्तकतया विशेषणविशेष्यभाव-संसर्गस्यान्यतरविशिष्टस्यान्यतरस्य तदैक्यस्य वा वाक्यार्थत्वाङ्गीकारे प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणविरोधाद्वाक्यार्थो न सङ्गच्छते । तदुक्तम् –
units.translation: The meaning of “That thou art” does not work like the meaning of “blue lotus.” In the latter, the quality blue, denoted by “blue,” and the substance lotus, denoted by “lotus,” exclude differences such as white cloth and the like, so it is acceptable to understand the sentence as expressing a relation of qualifier and qualified, one term qualified by the other, or their identity; no other means of knowledge contradicts this. Here, however, accepting the relation of qualifier and qualified between consciousness qualified by remoteness and consciousness qualified by immediacy, or accepting the identity of one with the other, conflicts with direct perception and other means of knowledge; therefore the sentence’s meaning would not work. This is stated in the following verse.

gloss.en: by excluding differences such as whiteness and cloth
of the relation of qualifier and qualified
of one qualified by the other
if accepted as the sentence meaning
because no other means of knowledge contradicts it
of consciousness qualified by remoteness and the like, the meaning of “That”
of consciousness qualified by immediacy and the like, the meaning of “thou”
of the relation of qualifier and qualified
of one qualified by the other
