units.label: Passage 24
units.deva:
“संसर्गो वा विशिष्टो वा वाक्यार्थो नात्र सम्मतः ।
अखण्डैकरसत्वेन वाक्यार्थो विदुषां मतः ॥" इति ॥२४॥
units.translation: “Neither a relation nor a qualified thing is accepted as the sentence’s meaning here. The wise hold that the sentence means an indivisible unity.”

units.label: Passage 25
units.deva:
अत्र गङ्गायां घोषः प्रतिवसतीतिवाक्यवज्जहल्लक्षणापि न सङ्गच्छते । तत्र तु गङ्गाघोषयोराधाराधेयभावलक्षणस्य वाक्यार्थस्याशेषतो विरुद्ध-त्वाद्वाक्यार्थमशेषतः परित्यज्य तत्सम्बन्धितीरलक्षणाया युक्तत्वाज् जहल्लक्षणा सङ्गच्छते ।
अत्र तु परोक्षापरोक्षचैतन्यैकत्वलक्षणस्य वाक्यार्थस्य भागमात्रे विरोधाद्भागान्तरमपि परित्यज्यान्यलक्षणाया अयुक्तत्वाज्जहल्लक्षणा न सङ्गच्छते । न च गङ्गापदं स्वार्थपरित्यागेन तीरपदार्थं यथा लक्षयति तथा तत्पदं त्वम्पदं वा स्वार्थपरित्यागेन त्वम्पदार्थं तत्पदार्थं वा लक्षयत्वतः कुतो जहल्लक्षणा न सङ्गच्छत इति वाच्यम् । तत्र तीरपदाश्रवणेन तदर्थाप्रतीतौ लक्षणया तत्प्रतीत्यपेक्षायामपि तत्त्वम्पदयोः श्रूयमाणत्वेन तदर्थप्रतीतौ लक्षणया पुनरन्यतरपदेनान्यतरपदार्थप्रतीत्यपेक्षाभावात् ॥२५॥
units.translation: The complete abandonment method, called jahallakṣaṇā, does not work here, as it does in the sentence “The village lives on the Ganges.” In that example, the sentence meaning—residence on the river itself—is wholly impossible and contrary, so abandoning it altogether and indicating the riverbank related to it is reasonable. Here, however, only one part of the sentence meaning—the identity of consciousness qualified by remoteness and immediacy—is contradictory. It would be unreasonable to abandon the remaining part as well and indicate something else; therefore complete abandonment does not work. One might object that, just as “Ganges” indicates the riverbank after giving up its own meaning, “That” or “thou” could indicate the meaning of the other word after giving up its own. That is not so: in the river example, the word “bank” is not spoken, so its meaning must be reached through implication; here, “That” and “thou” are both expressly spoken, so there is no need for one word to imply the meaning of the other.

gloss.en: of the Ganges and the village
characterized by the relation of support and supported
of indicating the bank related to it
of the identity of consciousness qualified as remote and immediate
by giving up its own meaning
by giving up its own meaning
because the word “bank” is not heard
when that meaning is not understood
because there is no need to understand the meaning of the other word

units.label: Passage 26
units.deva: अत्र शोणो धावतीतिवाक्यवदजहल्लक्षणापि न सम्भवति । तत्र शोणगुणगमनलक्षणस्य वाक्यार्थस्य विरुद्धत्वात्तदपरित्यागेन तदाश्रयाश्वादिलक्षणया तद्विरोधपरिहारसम्भवादजहल्लक्षणा सम्भवति । अत्र तु परोक्षत्वापरोक्षत्वादिविशिष्टचैतन्यैकत्वस्य वाक्यार्थस्य विरुद्धत्वात्तदपरित्यागेन तत्सम्बन्धिनो यस्य कस्यचिदर्थस्य लक्षितत्वेऽपि तद्विरोधपरिहारासम्भवाद् अजहल्लक्षणा न सम्भवत्येव । न च तत्पदं त्वम्पदं वा स्वार्थविरुद्धांशपरित्यागेनांशान्तरसहितं त्वम्पदार्थं तत्पदार्थं वा लक्षयत्वतः कथं प्रकारान्तरेण भागलक्षणाङ्गीकरणमिति वाच्यम्। एकेन पदेन स्वार्थांशपदार्थान्तरोभयलक्षणाया असम्भवात् पदान्तरेण तदर्थप्रतीतौ लक्षणया पुनस्तत्प्रतीत्यपेक्षाभावाच्च ॥२६॥
units.translation: The method of retaining the literal meaning, called ajahallakṣaṇā, also does not work here, as it does in the sentence “The red one runs.” There, the literal meaning “red” cannot run, so the word indicates the horse or another red thing that bears the quality, while retaining the quality red; this resolves the contradiction. Here, however, the identity of consciousness qualified by remoteness and immediacy is contradictory. Even if one retains the literal meanings and indicates some associated thing, the contradiction remains unresolved. One might say that “That” or “thou” can give up the incompatible part of its own meaning and, retaining the rest, indicate the meaning of the other word. This is not possible, because a single word cannot at once indicate its own remaining meaning and the meaning of another term; moreover, the other word is already expressly present, so there is no need to infer its meaning again.

gloss.en: the method of retaining the literal meaning
characterized by the red quality and running
by indicating the horse or another bearer of that quality
because that contradiction can be resolved
of the identity of consciousness qualified by remoteness, immediacy, and the rest
because that contradiction cannot be resolved
and it is not the case
by abandoning the incompatible part of its own meaning
of indicating both a part of its own meaning and another meaning
and because there is no need for another implication

units.label: Passage 27
units.deva: तस्माद्यथा सोऽयं देवदत्त इति वाक्यं तदर्थं वा तत्कालैतत्कालविशिष्टदेवदत्तलक्षणस्य वाक्यार्थस्यांशे विरोधाद् विरुद्ध-तत्कालैतत्कालविशिष्टांशं परित्यज्याविरुद्धं देवदत्तांशमात्रं लक्षयति तथा तत्त्वमसीतिवाक्यं तदर्थो वा परोक्षत्वापरोक्षत्वादिविशिष्टचैतन्यैकत्व-लक्षणस्य वाक्यार्थस्यांशे विरोधाद्विरुद्धपरोक्षत्वापरोक्षत्वविशिष्टांशं परित्यज्याविरुद्धम् अखण्डचैतन्यमात्रं लक्षयतीति ॥२७॥
units.translation: Therefore, just as the sentence “That is this Devadatta,” or its meaning, gives up the incompatible qualifications of past and present time because they conflict in one part of the sentence’s meaning and indicates only the non-conflicting Devadatta, so the sentence “That thou art,” or its meaning, gives up the incompatible qualifications of remoteness and immediacy and indicates only the non-conflicting, indivisible consciousness.

gloss.en: of Devadatta qualified by past and present time
the conflicting qualification of past and present time
of the identity of consciousness qualified by remoteness and immediacy
the conflicting qualifications of remoteness and immediacy

units.label: Passage 28
units.deva: अथाधुनाहं ब्रह्मास्मि इत्यनुभववाक्यार्थो वर्ण्यते । एवम् आचार्येणाध्या-रोपापवादपुरःसरं तत्त्वम्पदार्थौ शोधयित्वा वाक्येनाखण्डार्थेऽवबोधिते अधिकारिणोऽहं नित्यशुद्धबुद्धमुक्तसत्यस्वभावपरमानन्दानन्ताद्वयं ब्रह्मास्मीत्यखण्डाकाराकारिताचित्तवृत्तिरुदेति । सा तु चित्प्रतिबिम्ब-सहिता सती प्रत्यगभिन्नमज्ञातं परं ब्रह्म विषयीकृत्य तद्गताज्ञानमेव बाधते तदा पटकारणतन्तुदाहे पटदाहवदखिलकारणेऽज्ञाने बाधिते सति तत्कार्यस्याखिलस्य बाधितत्वात्तदन्तर्भूताखण्डाकाराकारिता चित्त-वृत्तिरपि बाधिता भवति । तत्र प्रतिबिम्बितं चैतन्यमपि यथा दीपप्रभादित्यप्रभावभासनासमर्था सती तयाभिभूता भवति तथा स्वयम्प्रकाशमानप्रत्यगभिन्नपरब्रह्मावभासनानर्हतया तेनाभिभूतं सत् स्वोपाधिभूताखण्डचित्तवृत्तेर्बाधितत्वाद्दर्पणाभावे मुखप्रतिबिम्बस्य मुख-मात्रत्ववत्प्रत्यगभिन्नपरब्रह्ममात्रं भवति ॥२८॥
units.translation: The meaning of the experience “I am Brahman” is now explained. After the teacher has clarified the meanings of “That” and “thou” by first teaching superimposition and rescission, and the student has been shown the indivisible meaning of the sentence, a mental modification shaped as indivisible reality arises: “I am Brahman, eternal, pure, awakened, liberated, real in nature, supreme bliss, infinite, and non-dual.” Containing a reflection of consciousness, that mental modification takes as its object the supreme Brahman, unknown and non-different from the inner Self, and removes the ignorance about it. When the ignorance that is the cause of everything is negated, all its effects are negated, just as cloth is destroyed when its causal threads are burned; the mental modification shaped as indivisible reality, which is included among those effects, is also negated. The reflected consciousness within it is overwhelmed by Brahman, just as a lamp’s light, unable to illumine sunlight, is overwhelmed by it. Since the mental modification cannot reveal the self-luminous supreme Brahman, non-different from the inner Self, the modification that served as its limiting adjunct is negated; then the reflected consciousness becomes nothing but that supreme Brahman, just as the reflection of a face becomes the face alone when the mirror is absent.

gloss.en: the meaning of the experiential sentence
with superimposition and rescission as the preliminary teaching
eternal, pure, awakened, liberated, real in nature, supreme bliss, infinite, and non-dual
when the threads that cause cloth are burned
because it is unfit to illumine
serving as its own limiting adjunct
of the reflection of a face
only supreme Brahman, non-different from the inner Self

units.label: Prose 46
units.deva: एवं च सति “मनसैवानुद्रष्टव्यम्", “यन्मनसा न मनुते" इत्यनयोः श्रुत्योरविरोधो वृत्तिव्याप्यत्वाङ्गीकारेण फलव्याप्यत्वप्रतिषेधप्रतिपादनात् । तदुक्तं
units.translation: Thus there is no conflict between the scriptural statements “It is to be seen by the mind alone” and “That which the mind does not think.” The teaching denies that Brahman is pervaded by the result of cognition, while accepting that it is pervaded by the mental modification. This is stated in the following verse.

gloss.en: by accepting pervasion by the mental modification
because the denial of pervasion by the result is taught

units.label: Prose 47
units.deva:
“फलव्याप्यत्वमेवास्य शास्त्रकृद्भिनिवारितम् ।
ब्रह्मण्यज्ञाननाशाय वृत्तिव्याप्तिरपेक्षिता” इति ॥
units.translation: “The teachers of scripture have denied that Brahman is pervaded by the result of cognition; for the destruction of ignorance about Brahman, pervasion by the mental modification is required.”

units.label: Prose 48
units.deva: “स्वयम्प्रकाशमानत्वान्नाभास उपयुज्यते" इति च ।
units.translation: “And because it is self-luminous, a reflection is not required.”

units.label: Prose 49
units.deva:
जडपदार्थाकाराकारितचित्तवृत्तेर्विशेषोऽस्ति । तथाहि अयं घट इति घटाकाराकारितचित्तवृत्तिरज्ञातं घटं विषयीकृत्य तद्गताज्ञान-निरसनपुरःसरं स्वगतचिदाभासेन जडं घटमपि भासयति । तदुक्तं 
"बुद्धितत्स्थचिदाभासौ द्वावपि व्याप्नुतो घटम् । 
तत्राज्ञानं धिया नश्येदाभासेन घटः स्फुरेत्” इति ॥
units.translation: There is a special distinction in the case of a mental modification shaped like an inert object. For example, a mental modification shaped like a pot takes the previously unknown pot as its object, removes the ignorance concerning it, and also illuminates the inert pot by the reflected consciousness within that modification. As the verse says: “Both the intellect and the consciousness reflected in it pervade the pot; there, ignorance is destroyed by the intellect, and the pot shines by the reflection.”

gloss.en: of a mental modification shaped like an inert object
a mental modification shaped like a pot
preceded by removing the ignorance concerning it
by the reflection of consciousness within itself
and the reflection of consciousness residing in it

units.label: Passage 29
units.deva: यथा दीपप्रभामण्डलमन्दकारगतं घटपटादिकं विषयीकृत्य तद्गतान्धकार-निरसनपुरःसरं स्वप्रभया तदपि भासयतीति ॥२९॥
units.translation: Just as the light of a lamp illuminates a pot, cloth, and other objects located in darkness, first removing the darkness present there and then making them shine by its own light.

gloss.en: the circle of a lamp’s light
a pot, cloth, and the rest

units.label: Prose 51
units.deva: एवंभूतस्वस्वरूपचैतन्यसाक्षात्कारपर्यन्तं श्रवणमनननिदिध्यासन-समाध्यनुष्ठानस्यापेक्षितत्वात्तेऽपि प्रदर्श्यन्ते। श्रवणं नाम षड्विध-लिङ्गैरशेषवेदान्तानामद्वितीयवस्तुनि तात्पर्यावधारणम् । लिङ्गानि तूपक्रमोपसंहाराभ्यासापूर्वताफलार्थवादोपपत्त्याख्यानि । यदुक्तं
units.translation: Up to the direct realization of consciousness as one’s own nature, the practices of hearing, reflection, deep contemplation, and samādhi are required; they are now explained. Hearing is the determination that all the Upaniṣads intend the non-dual reality, made through six indicators. These indicators are beginning and conclusion, repetition, uniqueness, result, praise, and reasoning. As the verse says:

gloss.en: until the direct realization of consciousness as one’s own nature
of the practice of hearing, reflection, deep contemplation, and samādhi
called beginning and conclusion, repetition, uniqueness, result, praise, and reasoning

units.label: Prose 52
units.deva:
“उपक्रमोपसंहारावभ्यासोऽपूर्वताफलम् ।
अर्थवादोपपत्ती च लिङ्गं तात्पर्यनिर्णये “ इति ॥
units.translation: “Beginning and conclusion, repetition, uniqueness, result, praise, and reasoning are the indicators for determining the intended meaning.”

units.label: Prose 53
units.deva: प्रकरणप्रतिपाद्यस्यार्थस्य तदाद्यन्तयोरुपपादनमुपक्रमोपसंहारौ यथा छान्दोग्ये षष्ठाध्याये प्रकरणप्रतिपाद्यस्याद्वितीयवस्तुन “एकम् एवाद्वितीयम्" इत्यादौ “ऐतदात्म्यमिदं सर्वम्”  इत्यन्ते च प्रतिपादनम् । प्रकरणप्रतिपाद्यस्य वस्तुनः तन्मध्ये पौनःपुन्येन प्रतिपादनमभ्यासः । यथा तत्रैवाद्वितीयवस्तुनि मध्ये तत्त्वमसीति नवकृत्वः प्रतिपादनम्। प्रकरणप्रतिपाद्यस्याद्वितीयवस्तुनः प्रमाणान्तराविषयीकरणमपूर्वता । यथा तत्रैवाद्वितीयवस्तुनो मानान्तराविषयीकरणम् ।
units.translation: Beginning and conclusion are the presentation of the subject matter of a text both at its opening and at its end. For example, in the sixth chapter of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad, the non-dual reality that is the topic is presented at the beginning in “One alone, without a second,” and again at the end in “All this has That as its Self.” Repetition is the repeated presentation of the topic throughout the text; there, for example, “That thou art” is taught nine times. Uniqueness is the fact that the non-dual reality taught by the text is not an object of any other means of knowledge; there, for example, the non-dual reality is not known through another means.

gloss.en: of what is taught by the text
of what is taught by the text
“all this has That as its Self”
of what is taught by the text
of what is taught by the text
not being an object of another means of knowledge
not being known through another means

units.label: Prose 54
units.deva:
फलं तु प्रकरणप्रतिपाद्यस्यात्मज्ञानस्य तदनुष्ठानस्य वा तत्र तत्र श्रूयमाणं प्रयोजनम्। यथा तत्र "आचार्यवान्पुरुषो वेद तस्य तावदेवं चिरं यावन्न विमोक्ष्येऽथ सम्पत्स्ये” इत्यद्वितीयवस्तुज्ञानस्य तत्प्राप्तिः प्रयोजनं श्रूयते । प्रकरणप्रतिपाद्यस्य तत्र तत्र प्रशंसनमर्थवादः । यथा तत्रैव "उत तमादेशमप्राक्ष्यो येनाश्रुतं श्रुतं भवत्यमतं मतमविज्ञातं विज्ञातम् ” इत्यद्वितीयवस्तुप्रशंसनम् । प्रकरणप्रतिपाद्यार्थसाधने तत्र तत्र श्रुयमाणा युक्तिरुपपत्तिः यथा तत्र “यथा सौम्यैकेन मृत्पिण्डेन सर्वं मृन्मयं विज्ञातं स्याद्वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयं मृत्तिकेत्येव सत्यम्“ इत्यादावद्वितीयवस्तुसाधने विकारस्य वाचारम्भणमात्रत्वे युक्तिः श्रूयते ।
मननं तु श्रुतस्याद्वितीयवस्तुनो वेदान्तानुगुणयुक्तिभिरनवरतम्
अनुचिन्तनम् ।
विजातीयदेहादिप्रत्ययरहिताद्वितीयवस्तुसजातीयप्रत्ययप्रवाहो निदिध्यासनम् ॥
units.translation: The result is the benefit stated in the text as arising from knowledge of its subject matter, or from practicing that knowledge. For example, it states that the benefit of knowing the non-dual reality is attaining it: “A person who has a teacher knows; for that person there is only so long until release, then he attains.” Praise is the commendation of the subject matter throughout the text. For example, “Have you asked for that teaching by which what was not heard becomes heard, what was not thought becomes thought, and what was not understood becomes understood?” Reasoning is the argument presented in the text to establish its subject matter. For example, the teaching that all transformations are only words and names, while clay alone is real, establishes the non-dual reality. Reflection is uninterrupted consideration of the non-dual reality taught by scripture, using reasoning that accords with Vedānta. Deep contemplation is a continuous flow of thoughts of the non-dual reality, free from thoughts about dissimilar things such as the body.

gloss.en: of what is taught by the text
“a person who has a teacher knows”
of knowledge of the non-dual reality
of what is taught by the text
in establishing the meaning taught by the text
by reasoning that accords with Vedānta
free from thoughts of dissimilar things such as the body
a continuous flow of thoughts of the non-dual reality

units.label: Prose 55
units.deva:
समाधिनिरूपणम्
समाधिर्द्विविधः सविकल्पको निर्विकल्पश्चेति । तत्र सविकल्पको नाम ज्ञातृज्ञानादिविकल्पलयानपेक्षयाद्वितीयवस्तुनि तदाकाराकारितायाश्चित्त-वृत्तेरवस्थानम् । तदा मृण्मयगजादिभानेऽपि मृद्भानवद्वैतभानेऽप्यद्वैतं वस्तु भासते । तदुक्तं
units.translation: Samādhi is of two kinds: with distinctions and without distinctions. The first is the abiding of a mental modification shaped like the non-dual reality, without requiring the dissolution of distinctions such as knower and knowledge. Even when the forms of a clay elephant and the like are seen, the clay alone is recognized; likewise, though duality appears, the non-dual reality shines. This is stated in the following verse.

gloss.en: without requiring the dissolution of distinctions such as knower and knowledge
when a clay elephant and the rest appear

units.label: Prose 56
units.deva:
"दृशिस्वरूपं गगनोपमं परं सकृद्विभातं त्वजमेकमक्षरम् ।
अलेपकं सर्वगतं यदद्वयं तदेव चाहं सततं विमुक्तमोम् " इति ॥
units.translation: “That which is of the nature of witnessing awareness, like the sky, supreme, shining by itself, unborn, one, imperishable, untainted, all-pervading, and non-dual—that alone am I, ever liberated.”

gloss.en: of the nature of witnessing awareness

units.label: Passage 30
units.deva: निर्विकल्पकस्तु ज्ञातृज्ञानादिविकल्पलयापेक्षयाद्वितीयवस्तुनि तदाका-राकारितायाश्चित्तवृत्तेरतितरामेकीभावेनावस्थानम् । तदा तु जलाकारा-कारितलवणानवभासेन जलमात्रावभासवदद्वितीयवस्त्वाकाराकारित-चित्तवृत्त्यनवभासेनाद्वितीयवस्तुमात्रम्  अवभासते । ततश्चास्य सुषुप्तेश्चाभेदशङ्का न भवति । उभयत्र वृत्त्यभाने समानेऽपि तत्सद्भावासद्भावमात्रेणानयोर्भेदोपपत्तेः ॥३०॥
units.translation: In nirvikalpa samādhi, without requiring the dissolution of distinctions such as knower and knowledge, the mental modification shaped like the non-dual reality abides in complete oneness with it. Then only the non-dual reality shines, just as only water appears when salt made into a figure dissolves in it and the salt is no longer seen. There should be no doubt that this state is different from deep sleep: although the mental modification is not separately manifest in either, the distinction between them is established by its presence in one and absence in the other.

gloss.en: without requiring dissolution of distinctions such as knower and knowledge
salt made into a figure in water
because it is not separately seen
because the mental modification shaped like the non-dual reality does not appear separately
in the non-manifestation of the mental modification
by the mere presence or absence of that

units.label: Passage 31
units.deva: अस्याङ्गानि यमनियमासनप्राणायामप्रत्याहारधारणाघ्यानसमाधयः । तत्र "अहिंसासत्यास्तेयब्रह्मचर्यापरिग्रहा यमाः" ।“शौचसन्तोषतपः-स्वाध्यायेश्वरप्रणिधानानि नियमाः" । करचरणादिसंस्थानविशेष-लक्षणानि पद्मस्वस्तिकादीन्यासनानि। रेचकपूरककुम्भकलक्षणाः प्राणनिग्रहोपायाः प्राणायामः । इन्द्रियाणां स्वस्वविषयेभ्यः प्रत्याहरणं प्रत्याहारः । लयविक्षेपाभावेऽपि चित्तवृत्तेर्रागादिवासनया अद्वितीय-वस्तुन्यन्तरिन्द्रियधारणं धारणा । तत्राद्वितीयवस्तुनि विच्छिद्य विच्छिद्यान्तरिन्द्रियवृत्तिप्रवाहो ध्यानम् । समाधिस्तूक्तः सविकल्पक एव ॥३१॥
units.translation: Its limbs are restraint, observances, posture, regulation of breath, withdrawal of the senses, concentration, meditation, and samādhi. Restraints are nonviolence, truth, non-stealing, continence, and non-possessiveness. Observances are cleanliness, contentment, austerity, study, and dedication to the Lord. Postures such as the lotus and svastika are defined by particular arrangements of the hands, feet, and other limbs. Regulation of breath is the means of controlling the breath through exhalation, inhalation, and retention. Withdrawal is drawing the senses back from their respective objects. Concentration is fixing the inner sense on the non-dual reality, even when sleep and distraction are absent but latent desires remain. Meditation is an uninterrupted stream of inner awareness directed to the non-dual reality. Samādhi has already been explained as the form with distinctions.

gloss.en: restraint, observances, posture, breath regulation, withdrawal, concentration, meditation, and samādhi
nonviolence, truth, non-stealing, continence, and non-possessiveness
cleanliness, contentment, austerity, study, and dedication to the Lord
defined by particular arrangements of hands, feet, and the rest
characterized by exhalation, inhalation, and retention
even in the absence of sleep and distraction
a stream of inner mental activity

units.label: Passage 32
units.deva: एवमस्याङ्गिनो निर्विकल्पकस्य लयविक्षेपकषायरसास्वादलक्षणाश्चत्वारो विघ्नाः सम्भवन्ति । लयस्तावदखण्डवस्त्वनवलम्बनेन चित्तवृत्तेर्निद्रा । अखण्डवस्त्वनवलम्बनेन चित्तवृत्तेरन्यावलम्बनं विक्षेपः। स्तब्धी-भावादखण्डवस्त्वनवलम्बनं कषायः । अखण्डवस्त्वनवलम्बनेनापि चित्तवृत्तेः सविकल्पकानन्दास्वादनं रसास्वादः । समाध्यारम्भसमये सविकल्पकानन्दास्वादनं वा ॥३२॥
units.translation: For one practicing this limb, nirvikalpa samādhi, four obstacles can arise: sleep, distraction, latent attachment, and savoring. Sleep is the mind’s lapse when its modification does not rest on indivisible reality. Distraction is the mind’s taking another support instead of indivisible reality. Latent attachment is the mind’s failure to rest on indivisible reality because it has become stiff or inert. Savoring is the mind’s enjoyment of the bliss of savikalpa samādhi even while it does not rest on indivisible reality; it can also be the enjoyment of that bliss at the very beginning of samādhi.

gloss.en: characterized by sleep, distraction, latent attachment, and savoring
because it does not rest on indivisible reality
because it does not rest on indivisible reality
because of becoming stiff or inert
even though not resting on indivisible reality
savoring the bliss of samādhi with distinctions
enjoying the bliss of samādhi with distinctions

units.label: Prose 60
units.deva: अनेन विघ्नचतुष्टयेन विरहितं चित्तं निर्वातदीपवदचलं सदखण्ड-चैतन्यमात्रमेववतिष्ठते यदा तदा निर्विकल्पकः समाधिरित्युच्यते । तदुक्तं
units.translation: When the mind is free from these four obstacles, it remains steady, like a lamp in a windless place, as indivisible consciousness alone. That state is called nirvikalpa samādhi. This is stated in the following verse.

gloss.en: like a lamp in a windless place

units.label: Passage 33
units.deva:
“लये सम्बोधयेच्चितं विक्षिप्तं शमयेत्पुनः । 
सकषायं विजानीयात्समप्राप्तं न चालयेत्
नास्वादयेद्रसं तत्र निःसङ्गः प्रज्ञया भवेत्“ इति
“यथा दीपो निवातस्थो नेङ्गते सोपमा स्मृता" इति च ॥३३॥
units.translation: “When the mind has lapsed, awaken it; when distracted, calm it again. Recognize it when it is colored by latent tendencies; when it reaches equilibrium, do not disturb it. Do not savor the taste there; become dispassionate through understanding.” The mind is also said to be “like a lamp in a windless place, which does not flicker.”

units.label: Prose 62
units.deva:
जीवन्मुक्तनिरूपणम्
अथ जीवन्मुक्तलणमुच्यते । जीवन्मुक्तो नाम स्वस्वरूपाखण्डब्रह्मज्ञानेन तदज्ञानबाधनद्वारा स्वस्वरूपाखण्डब्रह्मणि साक्षात्कृतेऽज्ञानतत्कार्य-सञ्चितकर्मसंशयविपर्ययादीनामपि बाधितत्वादखिलबन्धरहितो ब्रह्मनिष्ठः।
units.translation: The nature of one liberated while living is now stated. A jīvanmukta is a person firmly established in Brahman, free from all bondage because, through knowledge of indivisible Brahman as one’s own nature, Brahman is directly realized and ignorance is sublated; ignorance and its effects, accumulated action, doubts, mistaken notions, and the rest are thereby sublated as well.

gloss.en: an explanation of one liberated while living
through knowledge of indivisible Brahman as one’s own nature
in indivisible Brahman as one’s own nature
of ignorance, its effects, accumulated action, doubts, errors, and the rest

units.label: Passage 34
units.deva:
"भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः । 
क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरे " इत्यादिश्रुतेः ॥३४॥
units.translation: “The knot of the heart is broken; all doubts are cut away; and all actions are exhausted when the higher and lower Brahman is seen,” as scripture says.

units.label: Prose 64
units.deva: अयं तु व्युत्थानसमये मांसशोणितमूत्रपुरीषादिभाजनेन शरीरेणान्ध्य-मान्द्यापटुत्वादिभाजनेनेन्द्रियग्रामेणाशनया पिपासाशोकमोहादिभाजनेन अन्तःकरणेन च पूर्वपूर्ववासनया क्रियमाणानि कर्माणि भुज्यमानानि ज्ञानाविरुद्धारब्धफलानि च पश्यन्नपि बाधितत्वात्परमार्थतो न पश्यति । यथेन्द्रजालमिति ज्ञानवांस्तदिन्द्रजालं पश्यन्नपि परमार्थमिदमिति न पश्यति । “सचक्षुरचक्षुरिव सकर्णोऽकर्ण इव" इत्यादिश्रुतः । उक्तञ्च
units.translation: During periods of activity, the liberated one sees the body, a container of flesh, blood, urine, and feces; the group of senses, a container of blindness, weakness, and incapacity; and the inner organ, a container of hunger, thirst, sorrow, and delusion. The liberated one also sees actions being performed through prior tendencies and their fruits being experienced, provided those fruits have begun and do not conflict with knowledge; yet, because they have been sublated, the liberated one does not ultimately see them. It is like a person who knows a magic show: though seeing it, that person does not regard it as ultimately real. Scripture says, “with eyes, as though eyeless; with ears, as though earless.” This is also stated:

gloss.en: containing flesh, blood, urine, feces, and the rest
containing blindness, weakness, incapacity, and the rest
containing hunger, thirst, sorrow, delusion, and the rest
fruits already begun that do not conflict with knowledge

units.label: Passage 35
units.deva:
"सुषुप्तवज्जाग्रति यो न पश्यति द्वयं च पश्यन्नपि चाद्वयत्वतः ।
तथा च कुर्वन्नपि निष्क्रियश्च यः स आत्मविन्नान्य इतीह निश्चयः” ॥इति ॥३५॥
units.translation: “One who, while awake, does not see duality, like one asleep, and who sees it yet remains non-dual; who acts and yet is actionless—that one is the knower of the Self. There is no other, this is certain.”

units.label: Prose 66
units.deva: अस्य ज्ञानात्पूर्वं विद्यमानानामेवाहारविहारादीनामनुवृत्तिवच्छुभ-वासनानामेवानुवृत्तिर्भवति शुभाशुभयोरौदासीन्यं वा । यदुक्तं –
units.translation: Only those auspicious tendencies continue that were already present before this person’s knowledge, just as food, movement, and similar ordinary activities continue; alternatively, the person remains indifferent to both good and bad. As has been stated:

units.label: Passage 36
units.deva:
"बुद्धाद्वैतसतत्त्वस्य यथेष्टाचराणं यदि ।
शुनां तत्वदृशां चैव को भेदोऽशुचिभक्षण ॥“ इति ।
"ब्रह्मवित्त्वं तथा मुक्त्वा स आत्मज्ञो न चेतर" इति च ॥३६॥
units.translation: “If someone who understands the truth of non-duality acts as he pleases, what difference is there between dogs and those who see truth when it comes to eating impure things?” One is a knower of the Self only after giving up the conceit “I am a knower of Brahman”; otherwise, one is not.

gloss.en: of one who has understood the true nature of non-duality
the status of being a knower of Brahman

units.label: Passage 37
units.deva:
तदानीममानित्वादीनि ज्ञानसाधनान्यद्वेष्ट्रत्वादयः सद्गुणाश्चालङ्कारवदनु-वर्तन्ते । तदुक्तम्
“उत्पन्नात्मावबोधस्य ह्यद्वेष्टृत्वादयो गुणाः ।
अयत्नतो भवन्त्यस्य न तु साधनरूपिण ॥“ इति ॥३७॥
units.translation: At that time, the means to knowledge—such as humility—and good qualities—such as non-hatred—remain with the knower like ornaments. As the verse says: “For one whose knowledge of the Self has arisen, qualities such as non-hatred arise effortlessly; they are not themselves means to knowledge.”

gloss.en: for one whose knowledge of the Self has arisen

units.label: Passage 38
units.deva: किं बहुनायं देहयात्रामात्रार्थमिच्छानिच्छापरेच्छाप्रापितानि सुखदुःख-लक्षणान्यारब्धफलान्यनुभवन्नन्तःकरणाभासादीनामवभासकः संस्तदवसाने प्रत्यगानन्दपरब्रह्मणि प्राणे लीने सत्यज्ञानतत्कार्य-संस्काराणामपि विनाशात्परमकैवल्यमानन्दैकरसमखिलभेदप्रतिभास-रहितमखण्डब्रह्मावतिष्ठते । “न तस्य प्राणा उत्क्रान्ति”, “अत्रैव समवलीयन्ते", “विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते” इत्यादिश्रुतेः ॥३८॥
units.translation: What more need be said? For the mere continuation of bodily life, the knower experiences the fruits of past action—pleasure and pain—brought about by one’s own will, lack of will, or another’s will. Remaining the illuminator of the inner organ, its reflections, and the rest, when those experiences come to an end and the vital force dissolves into the inward blissful supreme Brahman, ignorance and even its residual impressions perish. The knower remains as absolute liberation, an indivisible Brahman whose nature is a single, undivided bliss, free from every appearance of difference. Scripture says, “His vital forces do not depart,” “Here they are completely dissolved,” and “having been freed, he is released.”

gloss.en: for the mere continuation of bodily life
brought about by one’s own will, lack of will, or another’s will
of the inner organ, its reflection, and the rest
when those come to an end
in the inward, blissful supreme Brahman
of ignorance, its effects, and residual impressions
having bliss as its sole essence
free from every appearance of difference

units.label: Prose 70
units.deva: ॥ इति श्रीसदानन्दयतिविरचितः वेदान्तसारः ॥
units.translation: Thus ends the Vedāntasāra composed by the ascetic Sadānanda.

gloss.en: composed by the venerable ascetic Sadānanda
